status: documentary audit complete; no new inference

observations: The author reports using Qwen3.8-27B Unsloth UD-Q3_K_XL for scripts and microservice diagnostics and sometimes UD-Q2_K_XL for more context.
The post gives no prompts, repository, model revision or hashes, runtime, hardware, verifier, or raw logs.
Comments conflict: reports of looping at Q8, a Q8 user reporting no loops with greedy decoding, and separate users attributing improvement to changed sampling, medium reasoning, or output limits.
Official thinking sampling: temperature 1.0, top_p 0.95, top_k 20, min_p 0, presence_penalty 0, repetition_penalty 1.
Supported reasoning_effort values are xhigh (default), medium, and low; the card warns that lower effort may reduce per-turn time but can increase failures and retries in multi-turn agent tasks.
The model card does not document a hard thinking-token budget.
One SGLang/GB10 user reports 20K-55K reasoning tokens and 45-80+ minute runs on large coding prompts.
A follow-up says explicit budgets plus temperature 0.6/top_p 0.95 worked for that user's BF16 setup; other comments disagree about root causes and fixes.
A separate 4-bit Mac report also describes long loops, but differs in hardware and runtimes.
sources.evidence_class: uncontrolled reports; not transferable benchmark evidence

observations: UD-Q3_K_XL and UD-Q2_K_XL are listed at approximately 13.1 GB and 9.83 GB.
The local AP-Q3_K_XL is a distinct file with separate calibration/encoding; it is not the Unsloth UD-Q3_K_XL from the Reddit post.

local_preflight.inference_decision: No new run: neither Reddit quant was available; the local AP-Q3 is a different calibrated artifact, and the available GPU snapshot did not establish an uncontended reservation. Do not stop ArtCraft or repurpose the production dual-GPU SOL profile.

conclusion: The material supplies a useful hypothesis for a future controlled loop/termination test, but no reproducible evidence to change profiles or sampling. Retain existing production settings. Any future test should use a fixed prompt set, score correctness and termination separately, include a hard token/output cap, and keep every run under the user's 30-minute cutoff.
